author: sjm41
body:
* **ARBA rule (ID and label):**
ARBA00051243

* **Sequences with problematic annotation (ID + gene/protein name):**
FBgn0032752	CG10702	(Q9VJ04)

* **Description of issue**
ARBA00051243 adds Rhea:10596 to CG10702.
RHEA is L-tyrosyl-[protein] + ATP = O-phospho-L-tyrosyl-[protein] + ADP + H+
However, the protein lacks a kinase domain and is therefore unlikely to be a kinase.

Seems to be based on these matches:
InterPro signature	IPR000494:Receptor L-domain
InterPro signature	IPR006211:Furin-like cysteine-rich domain
InterPro signature	IPR009030:Growth factor receptor cysteine-rich domain superfamily
title: ARBA2GO issue: ARBA00051243

author: Antonialock
body: I found a paper with some minimal phenotype characterization of a mutant, it's not much but I'll try and get the entry annotated for swiss-prot so at list this problem disappears. It would be good if ARBA could be a bit cleverer with signature selection...?

author: Antonialock
body: it doesn't seem completely crazy in a way, the paper investigated it as part of a kinase screen - it used to have an IBA to kinase activity...

author: sjm41
body:
Thanks Antonia!
No, it's not crazy at all, but it's still wrong!

author: Antonialock
body:
For sure. I added the caution "The protein was previously predicted to function as a protein kinase (Ref.4), but as it lacks a kinase domain it is unlikely to catalyze phosphotransfer".

Our late March release has been pushed back to early April, so hopefully this update should make it in.
